claims.text: Hafnium should be added to a CoCrFeNi-based HEA bond coat during alloy synthesis.
Adding Hf to the CoCrFeNi-based bond coat will improve coating durability and reliability.
Hf addition will promote formation of a continuous, thin, Hf-rich alumina scale.
A continuous, thin alumina scale will reduce oxygen diffusion and oxide spallation.
The untreated CoCrFeNi-based bond coat typically forms a heterogeneous scale dominated by Mn- and Cr-based oxides.
The untreated oxide scale grows non-uniformly and is prone to spallation.
Preliminary TEM/EDS studies can identify an Hf concentration that provides suitable segregation without unwanted phases.
The Hf-modified coating should remain effective during cyclic oxidation at 1100–1200°C in air or simulated turbine environments.
During high-temperature cycling, Hf segregates to the oxide–metal interface.
Interfacial Hf segregation promotes a denser and more adherent alumina scale.
The modified scale limits diffusion pathways for both oxygen and metal cations.
Limiting oxygen and metal-cation diffusion reduces oxidation rates and oxide spallation.
The Hf-doped bond coat will oxidize more slowly than the undoped baseline.
The Hf-doped bond coat will have better oxide-scale adhesion than the undoped baseline.
The Hf-doped bond coat will have a longer cyclic high-temperature service life than the undoped baseline.
Performance improvement requires an optimized Hf range that does not cause adverse phase formation or embrittlement.
The intervention may become less effective outside the tested temperature range or when the underlying alloy interacts unfavorably with Hf.
Reactive-element doping is known to improve oxide adherence in similar material systems.
